unit.meaning: U synapse-equivalents firing at the eye's full rate (150 Hz) hold a Shiu LIF cell at threshold in steady state (v_ss = w_syn * count * rate * tau_syn, the formula G1-gate s.5.1 used). Every stage's base counts are stated in U at gain 1.

weights.measured_pairs: unchanged: (type-2 count - type-1 count) x w_syn = 0.275 mV (Shiu), per synapse sign rule of G1
weights.bridge_edge_count: count = base x g_class (integer, > 0, excitatory, sign +1). The kernel sees an extra (pre, post, count) pair.
weights.collisions_with_measured_pairs: Network.from_pairs sums duplicate pairs. The derived edge list has 0 collisions (checked against all 24,921,936 measured pairs). Task B re-checks; if any appear, it lists them and the provenance module splits a merged pair's drive by count ratio. Colliding sources are never dropped.

stimulated_set.rule: B1 tectal segments present in the brain of record minus B1's never-stimulate exclusions (G1's removal of tectal cells with a direct synapse onto a readout is dropped)
stimulated_set.sha256_of: numpy uint64 array of the sorted segment ids, .tobytes()
stimulated_set.why: G1 removed tectal cells with a direct synapse onto a readout so that G1 could ask whether the wiring relays past hop 1. G1c asks how much of the decision the measured map carries, and a direct tectal contact is the most measured path there is, so the removal is dropped. This changes the eye protocol: the retina cache key and the W matrix change with the stimulated ids.
stimulated_set.eye_model: brain.Retina with RetinaParams() unchanged (OFF-transient centre-surround, 150 Hz, 5 ms frames). Its input is labelled 'chosen (eye model)' in provenance and never counted as measured wiring.

a.name: observed-origin tectal fragments
a.rule: Eligible = every segment in oa_fragments.json that is classed O-a1 on at least one deciding readout, is NOT a B1 tectal cell (O-a0 cells are tectal cells and receive the eye model directly), and has >= 1 INPUT synapse inside the tectum mask (roles.in.in_tectum >= 1). Output-only tectal ends are excluded because the signal direction there is unknown. Each eligible fragment F receives one bridge edge from each of the U = 34 stimulated B1 tectal somas nearest (3-D Euclidean, um; voxel 8 x 8 x 30 nm; ties by lower seg id) to F's tectal_end_8nm, in the lobe tectal_end_side. Base count 1 each (= 1 U at gain 1). F's own measured synapses (onto the readouts and everything else) are unchanged and keep Shiu's weight.
a.column_note: G1c-measure's 20-soma column was descriptive (it placed the columns on B1's map). 34 is chosen so that every stage is normalised to the same unit U; it is not a biological column size.

a.headline_note: Under the pre-registered metric a bridged link passes m = 0, so a fragment driven only through class-(a) links carries m = 0 downstream. Class (a) adds measured synapses to the path (synapse-count share) and not to the decision-path share.

b.name: tract topography
b.why: G1c-measure s.1: O-b is 24-30% of the M-system's input but also 15.5% of the caudal-hindbrain negative control's, so it is not specific; its median fragment stops 59-69 um short of the tectum; the mesh check agreed with the synapse clouds for 19 of 20. Assigning an unobserved origin is pure model with a lot of freedom, and under the metric it cannot raise the headline.
b.sensitivity_row_rule: Optional, never in the verdict, run only after the mandatory publications: O-b fragments on a deciding readout whose synapse cloud comes within 20 um of the tectum mask (min d_T <= 20 um, G1c-measure's post hoc near-tectum pool, 1.5-1.7% of M-system input). Each is linked like class (a): 34 nearest stimulated tectal somas to its closest-approach cloud synapse, lobe = side of that synapse, base 1. Gain g_b := the tuned g_a (not tuned separately).

c.name: literature relays and the midline crossing

E1_tectum_to_contra_M_system.sources: per lobe s, the stimulated tectal cell nearest each point of a 6 x 6 grid over the lobe's (u, v) map, points ((i + 0.5)/6, (j + 0.5)/6) (cells.lobe_coords; ties by lower seg id; duplicates merged)
E1_tectum_to_contra_M_system.targets: the three M-system cells (Mauthner, MiD2cm, MiD3cm; readouts.json task_criteria) on the side opposite lobe s
E1_tectum_to_contra_M_system.label: functional edge standing for an unidentified crossed pathway, not a claimed axon
E1_tectum_to_contra_M_system.literature: Dunn 2016 (a right-field loom evokes a leftward escape; M-system ablation perturbs only escapes contralateral to it; the paper leaves 'either a direct or indirect path from the OT'); Zottoli 1987 (tectal stimulation evokes PSPs in BOTH M-cells in goldfish; only the uncrossed one was localised, to the ventral dendrite); Helmbrecht 2018 (threat and approach tracts are uncrossed, so the crossing is downstream and unidentified).
E1_tectum_to_contra_M_system.why_no_relay: No source found identifies a hindbrain relay that carries tectal loom signals to the contralateral M-cell. Spiral fiber neurons (r3, atlas labels 29/32) are the only identified crossed excitatory input to the M-cell (Lacoste 2015), but were shown to respond to water puffs and taps, not to visual stimuli. Using them would add an unsupported tectum -> SFN claim and more edges.
E1_tectum_to_contra_M_system.why_grid: Dunn 2016 finds tectal ensemble activity encoding a critical image size (~72 deg). A sparse whole-lobe sample makes the M-system integrate stimulus size: at gain g, threshold needs about 34/g grid sources at full rate. Expected (not measured): a 3-deg prey reaches at most 1-2 grid sources, a large loom many.

P1_frontal_tectum_to_APN.sources: per lobe s, the stimulated tectal cell nearest each point of a 6-deg grid in (theta, elev) over the frontal zone theta <= 60 deg (B1's map: theta centres -17, -11, ..., 55; elevation centres 67, 61, ..., -65; 299 points; duplicates merged)
P1_frontal_tectum_to_APN.target: the APN relay of side s (ipsilateral)
P1_frontal_tectum_to_APN.label: tectum -> AF7-pretectum: required by ablation (Antinucci 2019 Fig 8), anatomy not shown; ipsilateral assumed
P1_frontal_tectum_to_APN.literature: Bianco & Engert 2015 (prey attended within about -60 to +60 deg, represented in the anterior tectum); Fajardo 2013 (anterior-ventral tectum stimulation evokes convergent saccades and J-turns); Antinucci 2019 (avOT-evoked hunting requires AF7-pretectal neurons).
P1_frontal_tectum_to_APN.why_dense: The approach pathway must detect a 3-deg object, so it pools a dense frontal sample (about 8.6 U at gain 1) where the escape pools a sparse whole-lobe one (about 1.06 U). The eye model has no size tuning; pooling density is the only size code available. The 6-deg spacing (2 x the 3-deg prey) is our choice.

P2_APN_to_nIII_dorsal_lateral_bilateral.targets: nIII_dorsal (readouts.json strict) members of BOTH sides whose lat_um >= the median lat_um of their side's dorsal pool (the lateral half), in the graph
P2_APN_to_nIII_dorsal_lateral_bilateral.literature: Antinucci 2019 (contra-projecting APN neurons put axon terminals bilaterally around nIII/nMLF); Dowell 2025 (a laterally located subset of medial-rectus motoneurons is active for hunting saccades and receives input from pretectal hunting command neurons).

P3_APN_to_nMLF_bilateral.targets: nMLF (strict) of both sides, in the graph
P3_APN_to_nMLF_bilateral.literature: Antinucci 2019 (collaterals around the nMLF); Gahtan 2005 (nMLF MeLr/MeLc are required for prey capture, in series with the tectum).

P4_APN_to_contra_turning_SPNs.targets: turning SPNs (RoV3 + MiV1 + MiV2, strict) on the side opposite the relay
P4_APN_to_contra_turning_SPNs.literature: Antinucci 2019 (contra-projecting cells end near ventral reticulospinal neurons in the contralateral hindbrain, and evoke contralaterally directed hunting); Huang 2013 (RoV3/MiV1/MiV2 fire for turns to their own side).
P4_APN_to_contra_turning_SPNs.conflict: Lau 2025 finds RoV3/MiV1/MiV2 minimally recruited in hunting J-turns (those use 'Mi3 lateral', 'Ca1 lateral', RoM2r, unlabelled in the Fish1 atlas). H2 scores these cells anyway, so this edge set is what makes H2's turn index readable; it is ours and disclosed.

c.relay_rule: APN relay of side s = the CAVE v709 soma nearest (um) to any AF7 voxel (mece3 label 3) on that side, among somas whose 4096-nm atlas voxel is mece2 14 (Pretectum) or 4 (Optic Tract and Accessory Optic System; Antinucci 2019 defines 'AF7-pretectum' as the ZBB masks 'Optic tract - AF7' and 'Griseum tectale (AF7)'), whose segment is in the graph and holds exactly one soma. One relay per side: the relay cells would share identical inputs, so more of them only split the output, and one cell is the minimum (Antinucci 2019: single-cell stimulation suffices).
c.relay_fallback: If mece3 cannot be fetched, the relay is the soma of those labels nearest the rostral pole of the tectum on that side. Not used: mece3 was fetched (sha256 above).

edge_list_sha256_of: json.dumps([[pre, post, base, sign, cls, pathway] for edges sorted by (cls, pathway, pre, post)], separators=(',', ':')) as UTF-8

gains.lower_bound_rule: 1 for every class: no class can be switched off by tuning.
gains.upper_bound_rule: 32 < U: no single base-1 bridge edge can hold its target at threshold alone at the eye's full rate.

tuning.what_moves: g_a and g_c only. Measured weights, LIF parameters, the eye model, every list in this file and every threshold are fixed.
tuning.stimuli: training set only (below). Controls and held-out stimuli never enter tuning.
tuning.search: the full 6 x 6 grid, every point evaluated and logged (time, gains, every training metric).
objective: 1. maximise the number of the 10 training checks passed: per stimulus side (left, right) - escape P >= 0.5; initiator on the stimulus side in >= 75% of escapes; first-spike disc angle >= 12 deg in >= 75% of escapes (the window enforces <= 100 ms after expansion ends); strike rule fires in >= 50% of prey trials; turn index toward the prey in >= 75% of prey trials
2. tie: minimise cross-talk on training stimuli (strikes on loom trials + escapes on prey trials)
3. tie: smallest g_c, then smallest g_a (the smallest bridge)
tuning.why_side_is_in_the_objective: The brief pre-registers that flee direction comes from the published pathway model when the crossing is built. A side-blind objective with a smallest-bridge tie-break would select the uncrossed measured path (class a) by construction and flee toward the threat; that is not what 'no tuning to hide' means. Honesty is kept by: gain floor 1 for every class, tuning seeds separate from gate seeds, the held-out hash check, and the per-class ablations published.
tuning.held_out_hash_check: every stimulus rendered during tuning is logged by sha256 of its parameter dict; the gate asserts that no held-out or control stimulus hash appears in the tuning log.
tuning.log: every evaluated grid point with ISO time, gains, metrics, network digest; the chosen point and the rule line that chose it.

controls.receding: G1's receding stimulus at +/-90 deg, l/v 240 (brain.stim_recede): 1,000 ms static onset window (reported, not scored), motion window scored
controls.dimming: G1's matched whole-field dimming, both eyes (brain.stim_dim)

stimuli.seed_rule: the same 8 seed strings in every gate condition (paired), as G1

readouts.escape: readouts.escape_decision over the six M-system cells (task_criteria): any spike in the window = escape; initiator = earliest first spike; escape direction = away from the initiator's side
readouts.strike: readouts.strike_decision (strict nIII_dorsal and nMLF pools as in readouts.json): the caller passes one spike count per member of readout_sets, and members that are not in the graph pass 0 (silent, still in the denominator); both nIII_dorsal pools >= 20% active and one nMLF >= 20% active; nMLF side index reported, not scored
readouts.turn: readouts.turn_index over strict turning SPNs (RoV3 + MiV1 + MiV2): TI = (mean R - mean L)/(sum); TI > 0 = right; undefined (no spikes) counts as not toward the prey
readouts.deciding_cells_for_the_headline: escape: the initiating M-system cell of each escape trial; strike: every nIII_dorsal and nMLF cell that spiked in the window; turn: every turning SPN that spiked

gate.source: G1b reopen gate (decision-brief agent, 2026-09-26), items H1, H2, C1-C3, L1, L2, verbatim, then our operationalisation

H1.verbatim: H1 Held-out loom escape (unseen l/v 120 and 480 ms; azimuths +/-45 and +/-135 deg; 8 paired seeds per condition): P(escape) is at least 0.5 per side. The first M-system cell to fire is the one on the stimulus side (Dunn 2016) in at least 75% of escapes. The first spike comes when the disc is at least 12 deg, and no later than 100 ms after expansion ends.
H1.scored: per stimulus side, pooled over that side's 4 held-out loom conditions (32 trials); every per-condition value published

H2.verbatim: H2 Held-out prey (unseen speeds of 15 and 60 deg/s; azimuths +/-15 and +/-45 deg): the strike rule (both dorsal-nIII pools at least 20% active, and at least one nMLF at least 20% active) fires in at least 50% of trials. The turning-SPN turn index points toward the prey in at least 75% of seeds. The nMLF side term is reported but not scored, because Lau 2025 finds the nMLF direction-insensitive.
H2.scored: per prey side, pooled over that side's 4 held-out prey conditions (32 trials); per-condition published

C1.verbatim: C1 Receding control, per side: mean Mauthner spikes are at most 0.5x the loom's, and P(escape) is lower.
C1.scored: receding motion window vs the same-side training loom (+/-90, l/v 240) run with the GATE seeds (those runs are a control baseline, not tuning); Mauthner = both Mauthner cells

C2.verbatim: C2 Dimming control: the same test against the mean of both looms. Report whether the eye model alone zeroes the tectal input; if it does, the item is recorded as passed by the eye, not by the brain.

C3.verbatim: C3 Blank control: no escape and no strike in at least 7 of 8 seeds, and no single turn direction in 75% or more of seeds.
C3.note: expected to pass by construction (no background input): labelled 'passed by construction'

L1.verbatim: L1 Bilateral M-system lesion (Mauthner + MiD2cm + MiD3cm, the task_criteria set; after Liu & Fetcho 1999): short-latency escapes fall to 0. Short latency means a first readout spike within 20 ms of the intact fish's median escape time; the 20 ms is our choice. The intact fish must escape in the same trials.
L1.run: held-out looms, 8 gate seeds, paired with intact trials
L1.note: passes by construction here (the escape readout is the lesioned set); the informative row published beside it = trials where any remaining deciding readout (turning SPN, nMLF, nIII) spikes within 20 ms of the intact median escape time

L2.verbatim: L2 Unilateral lesion: only escapes to the side opposite the lesion are removed (Dunn 2016). The 'union' lesion set (which covers the contested MiD3cm-left) is a sensitivity row.
L2.scored: left and right task_criteria M-system lesions separately on the held-out looms (8 gate seeds): escapes initiated on the lesioned side = 0 (by construction), and P(escape) for looms on the NON-lesioned side stays >= 0.5 (H1's own threshold) with the stimulus-side rule still >= 75%

verdict.PASS: H1, H2, C1, C2, C3, L1 and L2 all pass
verdict.KILL: the brief's only kill: not (H1 and H2 and C1 and C2 and C3), i.e. no correct escape or strike on held-out stimuli with the controls holding, even with the bridge
verdict.FAIL_NOT_KILL: H and C pass but L1 or L2 fails: published; the page may not say the gate passed

provenance.edge_flags: every bridge edge carries cls (a | c; b in the sensitivity row only), pathway id, base count and citation key (this file's 'edges'); measured pairs are cls 'measured'; the eye's Poisson input is 'chosen (eye model)'
provenance.network_digest: the bridged network's digest must fold in bridge_version, edge_list_sha256 and the gains, so it differs from the G1 digest and from any other gain setting; the JS kernel runs it as plain extra pairs

metrics.headline: decision-path share (brief, G1c section): drive-weighted mean m over the deciding cells, per readout and per condition, with the drive split into measured / bridge (a) / bridge (c) / eye (chosen)
metrics.secondary: synapse-count share, reported twice: (1) whole brain of record + bridge; (2) the exact reduced network the gate simulates. Both per class (edges and synapse-equivalents = base x gain).

mandatory_publications.M1_measured_shuffle_bridge_fixed: degree-preserving shuffle of the MEASURED pairs only (sim.shuffled_copy algorithm as G1), bridge edges re-added unchanged by segment id, gains fixed at the tuned values, stimulated set unchanged. 10 shuffles, seeds 'G1c-measured-shuffle-{k}' (k = 0..9; at least 5 if machine time forces it, disclosed), H1 and H2 held-out conditions with gate seeds G1-seed-0..3. Rule fixed now: if the shuffled fish's H1 and H2 pass/fail outcomes equal the intact fish's in >= 8 of 10 shuffles, the page says 'the anatomy is real; the decision runs through the model'. Per-shuffle metrics published either way.
mandatory_publications.M2_bridge_ablation: on the H1 and H2 held-out conditions with the 8 gate seeds: (i) all bridge edges removed (G1c stimulated set, measured wiring only); (ii) class (a) removed; (iii) class (c) removed; also (iv) E1 removed and (v) P1-P4 removed, as rows
mandatory_publications.M3_both_metrics_per_class: decision-path share and synapse-count share, per class and per readout, for the intact gate run and each ablation
mandatory_publications.M4_also: cross-talk table (strikes on loom trials, escapes on prey trials, per condition; reported, not scored); the tuning log; the held-out hash check; the disclosure sentence decision

expected_not_measured.decision_path_share: near 0 for escape, strike and turn: every stage that reaches a deciding cell passes through a bridge edge, and the metric gives a bridged link m = 0; measured-only paths carry walk weights of 1e-7 to 1e-5 (G1c-measure s.4).
expected_not_measured.disclosure: the crossing is built (E1), so the brief's pre-registered sentence applies: 'Which way the fish flees is set by the published pathway model, not by the measured wiring.'
expected_not_measured.proposed_parallel_sentence_not_preregist: 'Whether and which way the fish strikes is set by the published pathway model (Antinucci 2019), not by the measured wiring.'
expected_not_measured.onset_check: the two directly driven O-a0 tectal cells with Mauthner contacts (17057069410: theta -7.5, elev -41.9; 16670127295: theta 48.5, elev -58.5, oa_fragments.json column_field_deg) sit > 40 deg from the loom centre (+/-90, 0); and 2 synapses at 150 Hz give 2 x 0.275 x 0.15 x 5 = 0.41 mV steady state against 7 mV, so they cannot fire a Mauthner cell at loom onset.
expected_not_measured.class_a_direction: class (a) is uncrossed and lands on the M-cell ventral dendrite on the tectal lobe's own side, so if strong it drives escapes TOWARD the threat; its columns sit in the lower field (G1c-measure s.5), so it should matter only late in a loom.
expected_not_measured.gain_window: mean-field arithmetic in the spec note s.6 (steady state, eye rates estimated from G1's measured tectal spike counts): the prey pathway (P1-P4) works from g_c = 2; E1 fires on large looms from g_c = 1-2 (near the loom's end) and at about 55-70 deg by g_c = 8; a 3-deg prey is expected to fire the M-system only from g_c of about 16. Expected feasible window g_c = 2-8.
expected_not_measured.M1: behaviour is expected to be unchanged by shuffling the measured wiring (the bridge carries the decision).
